note: T_ready_total here contains T_exec + common outer residual only. T_plan is reported separately (joint 0.028-0.040s; greedy <0.1s) and T_pre is not measured on CPU.
detail: At the registered 47 GiB/card budget all six strategies return T_ready_total = 0.527781 s (all 66 extents in HBM; 32.75 GiB of demand against 47 GiB of capacity, 14.25 GiB headroom). Sweeping 8-47 GiB/card, the spread never exceeds 5.7 ms against a 100 ms threshold, so GATE2 fails at every point, including points where the cap genuinely binds (8 GiB/card = 75% of weights demoted). The only divergence anywhere is strong_simple, which stops 0.5 GiB short of the cap at 8-32 GiB/card and is 5.37-5.67 ms slower: 5.7% of the threshold and inside the model's own -0.19%..-6.04% error band. joint returns an optimal MILP solution at every point with no fallback, numerically identical to plain per-extent fastest-class fill.
audit_notes: Scoring identity is independent of the one-class-per-extent rule; only the SET identity depends on it. With the rule removed, fastest_seq/balanced add 66 dead duplicate copies at 47 GiB (132 rows) and score exactly the same.
The product MILP emits a redundant duplicate copy of one extent at 47 GiB (67 rows for 66 extents). Deduplicated to the fastest class the score is unchanged at 0.527781.

balanced was rewritten during this round: the first version had a byte-identical traversal order to fastest_seq and did not consult the scorer. It now equalises rank chain ends using the real timeline, and still converges to the same answer. Earlier 'balanced is 20-40% slower' readings were a harness turn-cap artifact and are withdrawn.
T_pre is not measured on CPU. T_plan is separate: joint 0.020-0.040 s, greedy selectors <=0.5 s wall for the whole sweep point.
